subject: Runaway queue / concurrency overspill — FastCommerce escalation
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara@fastcommerce.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Apr 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike in checkout latency + 502s — urgent

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in checkout p95/p99 starting ~07:45 PDT — p99 jumped from ~450ms to ~6s, and error rate (502/timeout) rose to ~1.8% on the checkout route. Throughput dropped roughly 30% despite normal traffic. No changes on our side. Attached are a small trace sample and the support dump.

Key notes:
- Spike correlates with a batch of long-context requests from our marketing experiment (many 12k tokens), but we can't be sure it's the sole cause.
- We see many in-flight requests getting queued and then timing out.

This is impacting checkout conversions and we need an ETA and mitigation. Please escalate — our Head of Ops is looped.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Li
Senior SRE, FastCommerce

Attachments:
- support_dump_20280407.zip (log snippets, sample traces)
- p99-graphs-08-12.png (stacked p95/p99 over last 2 hours)

Subject: Fwd: Sudden spike in checkout latency + 502s — urgent

Folks — forwarding FastCommerce. They report p99 ~6s, error spike and throughput degradation. Priority: investigate queueing/backpressure and concurrency caps. Quick triage checklist:

1) Concurrency cap hit? Verify per-tenant concurrency and any recent policy changes.
2) Queue depth & backpressure metrics (per-route request_queue_size, worker_saturation).
3) Batching window behavior — are long-context requests forcing large batches / delaying small requests?
4) Model fallback behavior and any routing changes in last 24h.
5) KV cache pressure / memory pressure on the serving hosts.

If this is a model-size / token-length distribution issue we should consider routing long-context requests to a larger instance pool or temporarily reducing batch window to favor latency. Hannah / Dev — can you grab the dashboard links and a short summary ASAP? I'll coordinate comms with FastCommerce and propose mitigations.

---
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Apr 2028 08:39:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden spike in checkout latency + 502s — urgent

Quick update from ops - pulled traces and infra metrics:

- We are seeing per-tenant concurrency at the configured cap of 16 for FastCommerce on the checkout route; bursts pushed many requests to the queue.
- Request size distribution shifted: ~12% of requests in the spike window had >8k tokens. Those long requests cause KV cache churn and larger GPU memory working sets.
- Batching: the continuous batching heuristic expanded batch windows due to mixed sequence lengths, leading to head-of-line blocking for small requests.
- Worker saturation on pool redwood-prod-g4-high-3: CPU and GPU utilization high, swap activity on one host indicating memory pressure.

Immediate mitigations I started (08:30):
- Increased per-tenant concurrency cap to 24 for the FastCommerce route (temp) — reduces queue depth but increases risk of OOM on small hosts.
- Forced long-context requests to the dedicated larger instance pool (redwood-prod-g8) by applying a routing tag for tokens >6k.
- Reduced batch aggregation window from 60ms -> 30ms for the checkout route to reduce batching head-of-line waits.

Preliminary result: queue length dropped ~65% in 5m and p99 improved to ~1.2s in the short term. Still watching for errors from memory pressure.

Next steps:
- Hannah, can you run a quick memcheck on the g4 host showing swap and confirm if any OOMs occurred?
- Marissa/Dylan, please update FastCommerce with the mitigations and the plan (we should offer a credit if they request).

-Dev
(Attachment: triage_snippets.txt)

Looping in our Head of Ops (andrew) and will escalate internally if we don't get a firm plan.

Cc: sara@fastcommerce.com, andrew.tan@fastcommerce.com
Date: Sat, 7 Apr 2028 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runaway queue / concurrency overspill — FastCommerce escalation

Team — thanks for the fast triage. Summary & plan to close this with FastCommerce by EOD: 

1) Short-term (already in motion) — Dev's mitigations: increased cap ->24, route >6k tokens to g8, reduce batch window to 30ms. Those have brought p99 from ~6s -> ~1.2s. Continue monitoring for 2 hours.

2) Near-term (this week) — Engineering will:
- Harden routing rules to proactively send long-context workloads to larger instance pools.
- Add a guardrail: when long-context traffic >5% of route for >15m, auto-scale or temporarily tighten batch window.
- Run a memory-profile sweep on the affected g4 host; if swap happened, repro and fix memory leak or increase instance size on that pool.

3) Durable fix (roadmap item) — Product/Infra: support a per-route QoS policy that prevents head-of-line blocking between microbursts of long and short sequences (likely by prioritizing small requests or lane separation). Estimate: planning next sprint, delivery Q2.

4) Commercial response — Offer FastCommerce a 1-week service credit tied to the observed conversion loss; Dylan, please propose the credit amount with PMM. We'll make this contingent on verification of impact and sign-off from Finance.

Owners: Dev (Dev Patel) — triage & memcheck; Hannah — telemetry artifact + postmortem; Dylan/Marissa — customer comms & credit negotiation. Rishi — loop for capacity planning and SLA guardrails.

I'll draft an executive note for FastCommerce with the timeline and the mitigation summary. Please add any input to the draft by 14:30 PDT.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
